Let \(P=(x,y)\). Since
\[
\overrightarrow{PF_1}=(-\sqrt5-x,-y),\qquad \overrightarrow{PF_2}=(\sqrt5-x,-y),
\]
the condition \(\overrightarrow{PF_1}\cdot \overrightarrow{PF_2}=0\) gives
\[
(-\sqrt5-x)(\sqrt5-x)+y^2=0
\]
so
\[
x^2-5+y^2=0 \implies x^2+y^2=5.
\]
Using the hyperbola \( \frac{x^2}{4}-y^2=1\), we have \(y^2=\frac{x^2}{4}-1\). Substitute:
\[
x^2+\frac{x^2}{4}-1=5 \implies \frac54x^2=6 \implies x^2=\frac{24}{5}.
\]
Then
\[
y^2=\frac{24/5}{4}-1=\frac65-1=\frac15.
\]
Thus the height from \(P\) to the \(x\)-axis is
\[
|y|=\frac1{\sqrt5}.
\]
The base \(F_1F_2=2\sqrt5\), so
\[
[F_1PF_2]=\frac12\cdot 2\sqrt5\cdot \frac1{\sqrt5}=1.
\]
\[
\boxed{1}
\]
